blocks.text: Why agile coaches choose Linear on Mac

Agile coaching is about removing friction from the development process. Legacy tools often add more friction than they remove. Linear on Mac is different because it prioritizes speed and simplicity. You spend less time clicking through nested menus and more time analyzing team data. The app is a native wrapper that feels right at home on macOS. It handles keyboard shortcuts better than any browser tab ever could.
Essential shortcuts for the daily coach

If you want to move fast, you must stop using your mouse for everything. Linear is built for the command palette. Press ⌘K to open the command menu. From here, you can search for any issue, change a status, or move a ticket to a different team. Press C to create a new issue instantly. Use P to set the priority. These small actions add up over a full day of sprint planning or backlog grooming.

items: ⌘K: Open the command palette to find anything.
C: Create a new issue without leaving your current view.
P: Change the priority of a selected issue.
Shift + D: Set a due date for a task.
?: Open the full list of keyboard shortcuts.

blocks.text: Coaches often struggle with visibility. Linear uses cycles to track sprint progress. You can create a cycle in the sidebar to group issues by time period. This helps you monitor velocity and see which items are at risk. If you are struggling with the setup, ask Lazur to guide you through creating your first cycle. You can also save custom views to filter by assignee or status. This keeps your focus on the work that matters most during standup meetings.

One common mistake is treating Linear like a traditional ticket system where items go to die. Linear is a living document of your team's work. If you do not keep statuses updated, your data will be useless for retrospective analysis. Another mistake is creating too many teams. Keep your workspace simple. Start with one or two teams to avoid fragmented views. If you find yourself lost in the settings, take a breath and use the command palette to find your way back to the inbox.

Linear plays well with Slack and GitHub. You can link pull requests directly to issues. This creates a clear trail for your team. You do not need to hunt for status updates when they are linked in the issue sidebar. Press ⌘I to show the details sidebar. This is where you will see linked PRs and recent activity. It is the best way to keep your team accountable without constant pings in Slack.
How to handle scaling and roadmapping

As your organization grows, issue-level tracking is not enough. You need to see the big picture. Use the Projects feature in Linear to track long-term goals. Projects allow you to group multiple issues together. This is perfect for quarterly planning. You can set target dates and monitor progress across multiple cycles. If you need to report to stakeholders, these project views are much cleaner than a spreadsheet.

Linear on Mac runs as a dedicated app. This means you can use your Mac's native features to stay organized. Use Stage Manager to keep Linear in a group with your other coaching tools like Miro or Slack. This prevents context switching fatigue. If you have multiple accounts, you can manage them within the app settings. Always check for updates to ensure you have the latest performance improvements.

faq.question: Is Linear available on the Mac App Store?
faq.answer: No, Linear is not in the Mac App Store. You must download it directly from linear.app/download.

faq.question: What are the system requirements for Linear on Mac?
faq.answer: The Linear desktop app requires macOS 12 or later to run.

faq.question: Can I use Linear for free?
faq.answer: Linear has a free plan, but it is limited to 2 teams and 250 non-archived issues.

faq.question: How do I find keyboard shortcuts in Linear?
faq.answer: Press the ? key inside the app to see a searchable list of all available keyboard shortcuts.
